feature: HUD 真實資料與成本提示
notes: Full-window game screen: top bar with four stocks, population (reserved shown in its tooltip), age and game clock straight from the Worker projection; bottom HUD with a 5x3 command grid, selection panel (portrait, HP, attack, range, cargo, status; group portraits; building HP, progress, queue with progress bars) and minimap. Icons are renders of the game's own brick models. Hover or focus shows a card with name, hotkey, cost (short resources marked), time, population and the disabled reason. Enemy selection/inspection and per-player score are not implemented.

Select a building to see its production list (names and costs from the ruleset), per-item disabled reasons from the shared trainBlocker, queue with progress and cancel buttons, rally point via right-click. Production tiles take Q W E R T in order; a researched age leaves the grid. Queue reordering is not implemented. v29: production tiles take Q W E R T A D Z X C V B Y (13). The villager build grid has two pages (first and second age; third age) switched by N or the page tile; a building's letter works from either page and turns to it (FU29-6). Technology cards list the Effect texts. A hovered production tile no longer throws when Esc deselects its building (FU29-5).

Shortcuts ignored in inputs/textareas/selects; context menu suppressed on the scene only; drag ending over the top bar uses pointer capture and presses nothing; the game page never scrolls, arrows always pan; the menu pauses the match and only Esc/F10 work while it is open; blur cancels a drag; background tab/blur pauses the sim. IME composition not separately tested.

Stock changes only through deposits (and existing reservations); cumulative ledger extracted = deposited + carried is asserted every tick in tests. HUD reads the Worker projection of the own account only.

toSource -> gathering -> toDropoff -> deposit -> resume, carry 10, deterministic per-tick progress; move/stop end work but keep cargo; a gather order for another resource returns cargo first; depletion returns cargo then switches to the nearest same-yield source within 600 or idles. Villager pose/tool follow the sim state.

feature: 合法 dropoff 與工作站位
notes: Work slots: walkable nodes within 50 of the resource footprint (same rule as the map generator). v19 drop-offs (dropoffRules, design_default): the town centre takes everything, lumber camp wood, mining camp gold and stone, mill food; only completed own buildings count, and a carrier walks to the nearest ring node of any accepting one. Upgrades that raise carry or gather speed not implemented.
Trees, stone and gold gathered with design_default rates (1 per 20/25/25 ticks); exhausted nodes free their navigation ground. Upgrades and tool technologies not implemented.

Sheep, deer and boar are units (GAIA until found; sheep change hands by proximity). Villagers hunt (strike, deer flee, boar charges) and gather the carcass; carcasses spoil slowly; shore fish are worked from land. Fishing ships, docks and fish traps are not implemented. v30: docks (on water by the shore), fishing ships (shore and deep fish, villagers' fishing pace, carry 10, drop-off at own docks only, no villager gather or carry technologies; Gillnets and the Japanese bonus apply) and fish traps (laid and worked by fishing ships only, 1000 food, owner only, gone when worked out; no reseed queue).

Farm: building (wood 60, 200x200, walkable), becomes an owner-only food source of 250 on completion; farmers stand on the field; worked out or destroyed removes it. Automatic reseeding (mill toggle, default on): the farmer who works a field out lays a new one on the spot for 60 wood, builds it and farms it; a farm's builder farms it.

13 economic technologies (Loom, Wheelbarrow, Hand Cart, lumber/gold/stone upgrades, Horse Collar, Heavy Plow, Crop Rotation). Gather rate in hundredths per tick with carried remainder; effects apply to work under way. Villager speed bonuses omitted (speeds must divide 50). v29: the divide-50 constraint on speeds is gone (speeds to a hundredth with carried remainder), but the Wheelbarrow and Hand Cart villager speed bonuses are still not implemented. Treadmill Crane (University) speeds construction +20%.

v30: market buy/sell of 100 food, wood or stone for gold at fair prices shared by both players (start 100/100/130, moving 2 a lot, 20-9999), fee 30% (Guilds 15%, Saracens 5%), rounded to whole gold; ledger.market. Tribute, Coinage and Banking are not implemented (one player a side, no allies).

House and barracks placement on the 50-unit grid: inside map, explored, buildable and level tiles, no overlap with obstacles, no unit body inside. Rotation, walls and docks not implemented. v30: walls are dragged as a straight line of one-tile segments (build.to, up to 24, each validated and paid on its own); gates may replace the owner's wall segment of the same material; docks stand wholly on water or shallows with a tile next to buildable land, fish traps anywhere on water; nothing is built over a gate, fish trap or farm (full extent). Rotation is still not implemented.

feature: 多工人施工與取消退款
notes: Cost reserved at placement (execution tick), committed on completion; cancel refunds 100% (economyRules.cancellationRefundPercent) and frees the ground. Builders stand on the ring outside the foundation; each adds 1 work/tick (required = entry time x tick rate). Same-tick overspend refused at execution with a logged reason.

Cap = min(40, completed housing: town center 5, house 5). Training reserves population when queued (refused with 人口已滿 x/cap when used+reserved would exceed cap), commits on spawn, refunds on cancel. Unit death and building loss not implemented.

feature: 生產佇列／集結點／堵出口
notes: Queue of up to 5 per building; only the first item advances (1 work/tick, required = entry time x tick rate); cost and population reserved at enqueue, full refund on cancel. Finished units spawn on the free ring node nearest the rally point (or the front); with every exit node occupied the item waits at 100% and spawns once one frees. Rally point per building, new units walk there. Reordering the queue not implemented.

Ages researched at the town center in sequence (age-2 -> age-3 -> age-4, design_default costs); one research of a kind at a time per player. v20: buildRequirement checks both ages and finished own buildings from the rule data, shared by the Worker and the page: the stable and the archery range need the second age and a finished barracks (reference prerequisite, medium-confidence source in aoe2-rules-research.md). Archers need the second age and train at the archery range. Own buildings render in the new age. No building prerequisites for advancing and no stat upgrades per age yet.

v27: stacking rules exist for civilization effects only (adds sum, multipliers multiply, age tiers replace each other, unique technologies in their Castle); a general technology graph with mutual exclusion is not implemented. v29: 22 generic technologies (University 8; barracks, archery range, stable, town centre and monastery 2-3 each; Castle 3) researched at their building after their age and prerequisite (Architecture after Masonry, Keep after Guard Tower, Town Patrol after Town Watch); their effects are Effect records in packages/content/techs.ts that packages/sim/civ.ts adds to every civilization's list, so they stack with civ bonuses by the same rules (adds sum, multipliers multiply) and enter rulesetHash. Chemistry is a prerequisite of the hand cannoneer and bombard cannon. Mutually exclusive technologies are still not implemented. v30: the dock's (War Galley, Galleon, Fast Fire Ship, Heavy Demolition Ship, Elite Cannon Galleon, Elite Longboat, Gillnets, Careening, Dry Dock, Shipwright), the market's (Caravan, Guilds) and the University's remaining technologies (Heated Shot, Fortified Wall, Bombard Tower) with their effects; War Galley upgrades three lines at once; buildRequirement checks a technology prerequisite (the bombard tower). New effect kinds marketFee, transportCapacity, arrowBonus.

Playable buildings: town center (start), house, barracks (militia), farm, lumber camp, mining camp, mill, stable (scouts), archery range (archers), monastery (monks, third age). Archery range wood 175 matches a medium-confidence reference source; other costs, all times and hit points are design_default. Blacksmith, market, dock, towers, walls and castle are inspector models or absent. v27: the Castle (third age, 300 stone and 60 s design_default against 650 stone on aoetw.com, 800 hp, 4x4, houses 10, holds 20, four arrows) trains unique units and researches unique technologies; the neutral Settlers have none. v29: the University (third age, wood 200, 40 s design_default against 60 s on aoetw.com, 3x3 against 4x4, 350 hp against 2100) researches the eight University technologies and trains nothing; villager tile U on the build grid's third-age page. Masonry and Architecture add +10% hp and +1/+1 armor to every building each (building armor is now per owner: stats.ts buildingTargetOf); Guard Tower and Keep x1.47 and x1.5 tower hp (250 -> 368 -> 551); Hoardings x1.21 Castle hp. v30: every remaining building of the 13 civilizations' trees: a second town centre from the third age (275 wood 100 stone), market, dock, fish trap, outpost (sight by age), palisade and stone walls, palisade gate and gate, bombard tower (after its University technology), wonder (wood 1000 gold 500 stone 500 scaled to this map). Build times about the site's / 2.5, hit points about the site's / 6 (design_default).

v30: palisade and stone walls (one-tile segments dragged as a line, each paid on its own; builders move on to the nearest unfinished segment within 300), palisade gate and gate (one tile, no blocking rectangle; closed to the enemy by a per-player gate overlay in movement.ts, open to the owner; can replace the owner's wall segment of the same material), Fortified Wall, the Chinese Great Wall on walls and gates. Gates cannot be locked, are 1x1 and do not rotate; walls, gates and the wonder cannot be converted. Diplomacy is not implemented.

Town centres (15) and watch towers (5) take villagers, foot soldiers, archers and monks; units inside heal, add an arrow each (villagers and archers), come out on an order or when the building falls or changes sides. Town bell with back-to-work. Garrison in rams and other buildings not implemented. v27: the Castle holds 20 (foot units only; villagers and foot archers inside add an arrow each); Teutons double tower garrison (10) and add 10 to town centres (25). v29: Herbal Medicine (monastery) makes units inside the owner's buildings heal 6 hit points every 40 ticks instead of 1, spread evenly (floor(tick x 6 / 40) steps, FU29-2); Teutons get it free. v30: the bombard tower holds 5 but those inside add no shots; transports carry land units like a garrison (naval.ts). Docks hold nobody.

Melee and pierce attacks against [melee, pierce] armor; damage = max(1, attack - armor + class bonuses). Buildings have armor [0,2]. Values design_default. v29: building armor depends on the owner's Masonry and Architecture (+1/+1 each; damageOn reads buildingTargetOf). New effect kinds: bonusScale (Siege Engineers x1.2 of the bonus against buildings) and class bonuses from Arson (+2 infantry) and Sappers (+15 villagers) against buildings.

Spearman (+12 vs cavalry), skirmisher (+4 vs archers, +3 vs spearmen, pierce armor 3), archer (+3 vs spearmen), knight (heavy cavalry). The computer answers seen cavalry with spearmen and seen archers with skirmishers.

Range (Chebyshev: 50 melee, 250 archer) and fixed cooldown ticks (20/30). Ranged units stop and shoot inside range. No minimum range. Hits are instant; no projectiles. v28: minimum ranges (mangonel 150, scorpion 100, trebuchet 200): automatic fights skip targets inside it and drop a target that comes inside; an ordered attack walks back out to firing distance (approach takes a minimum). Siege ranges 150 + 50 a tile (mangonel and scorpion 500, onager 550, trebuchet 950), archers keep 50 + 50 a tile; siege and melee cooldowns = seconds x10, ranged x15. v29: correction to the v28 note: siege ranges are 50 + 50 a tile like archers (mangonel and scorpion 400, onager 450, trebuchet 850). Siege Engineers +50 range to siege except the ram line; hand cannoneer 400; bombard cannon 650 with a 250 minimum (Turks' Artillery +100); Thumb Ring cooldown /1.18 foot archers, /1.11 cavalry archers (Mangudai included), /1.25 Chu Ko Nu.

v28: blast (mangonel 75, onager 90, siege onager 110; Warwolf trebuchet 75): every enemy unit within the radius of the impact (the target's centre or a building's footprint) takes the full hit with its own armor. Pass-through (scorpions): enemy units within 25 of the line from the shooter to 200 past a unit target take half the attack, those between shooter and target included. Own units are never hit (design_default; aoetw says mangonels hurt own units). No ground attack. v29: bombard cannon blast 50 (one node; aoetw 0.5 tile; 25 reached only the target itself, FU29-4). v30: the demolition raft line (blast 125/150/175) uses the petard's self-destruct and the blast rule against units and buildings.

Idle militia and archers engage enemies within their engage radius; villagers, scouts and monks fight only when ordered (monks never attack). v21 fix: a building target's visibility used a 16-wide tile index on every map, so on the 32x32 map attacks on buildings were accepted or cancelled by unrelated tiles (regression test in combat.test.ts). v21: a remembered enemy building in the fog can be targeted (as in the reference); if it is already gone the order is still accepted and becomes a walk to the remembered spot, so nothing leaks. Unit targets must be visible. No stances.

Battering ram from the siege workshop (third age, needs a blacksmith): buildings only (+40), pierce armor 120, speed 2. Mangonels, scorpions, trebuchets (pack/unpack) not implemented. v28 (replaces the last sentence): mangonel and scorpion lines from the siege workshop, Capped and Siege Ram upgrades; the trebuchet (Castle, fourth age) unpacks 150 ticks (7.5 s) on the spot before its first shot and packs 150 ticks before its first step (State.setups); stopping a half-done packing to shoot again resets it (FU28-1). Rams and trebuchets are buildingsOnly and never pick a target by themselves. Kataparuto: setup x0.25. The Worker projects UnitView.unpacked (stride 19); the model switches between a packed wagon and a standing frame without a packing animation. One trebuchet armor set [1,8] in both states.

Death removes the unit, frees population, records carried cargo as lost (ledger extracted = deposited + carried + lost), cancels its work and leaves a 40-tick corpse for the death pose. Destroyed buildings free their ground, recompute housing and forfeit foundation/queue money (reserved population released).

Six unit-line upgrades (Man-at-Arms, Long Swordsman, Pikeman, Crossbowman, Elite Skirmisher, Light Cavalry) and 15 blacksmith technologies; units in the field take new numbers at once. Siege, gunpowder, cavalry archers, camels and later lines not implemented. v27: 13 unique units with elite upgrades (the Janissary and Mangudai are the only gunpowder and cavalry-archer units); generic gunpowder, cavalry-archer and camel lines remain absent. v28: cavalry archer, camel rider, mangonel, scorpion, trebuchet and petard, and 14 fourth-age line upgrades (Two-Handed Swordsman, Champion, Halberdier, Arbalester, Heavy Cavalry Archer, Hussar, Cavalier, Paladin, Heavy Camel Rider, Capped Ram, Siege Ram, Onager, Siege Onager, Heavy Scorpion) researched at the unit's building after the step before; costs and times from aoetw.com, stats converted (docs/aoe2-rules-research.md 單位). Camels are their own class; the spear line gained camel bonuses; blacksmith melee attack and barding reach camels. Still absent: naval and gunpowder units, other civs' unique units, expansion-only units (e.g. Imperial Camel Rider); the computer trains none of the new units. v29: hand cannoneer (archery range) and bombard cannon (siege workshop), fourth age after Chemistry; costs and times from aoetw.com, stats converted (docs/aoe2-rules-research.md 科技). No accuracy model: every shot hits. Generic technologies that change unit numbers: Chemistry, Siege Engineers, Squires, Arson, Thumb Ring, Parthian Tactics, Bloodlines, Husbandry, Fervor, Sappers, Supplies (cost), Conscription (training time). v30: ships on the water layer: fishing ship, transport ship, trade cog, galley line, fire galley line, demolition raft line, cannon galleon (+elite) and the Viking longboat; trade cart. Ships approach on their own layer; only units with range 150 or more engage across the shore; units with attack 'none' refuse attack orders. No accuracy model.

v30: warships trained at the dock and leaving it on the water side; galley, fire and demolition lines, cannon galleon, longboat; transports load and unload, a sunk transport kills its passengers. Repair (of ships, docks or any building) is not implemented.

v30: trade carts loop between their nearest own market and the other player's market, trade cogs between docks; gold per round trip round(D*(D/S+0.3)*1.4) (cog x0.75; D tiles between the buildings, S the map side; after the AoE II community formula, scaled, design_default), paid on return home (ledger.trade); Caravan +50% speed.
v30: a trade route ends when either end falls or changes hands, the unit changes sides, any other order is given, or the route is unreachable 3 times. Diplomacy is not implemented.

Monastery (third age, wood 175) trains monks (gold 100, 30 hp). v22 conversion as in the reference research: one attempt per 24 ticks (1.2 s; sources conflict with 1 s), attempts 1-3 fail, then 28% each (seeded generator), the 10th always succeeds. Heal: own wounded non-monk units, range 150, 1 hp per 20 ticks, automatic when idle (rate and ranges design_default). The computer trains up to 2 monks, converts enemies within 700 of its town centre and fetches relics.

v22: Redemption (buildings except town centre, monastery, farm; adjacent; 18-30 s), Atonement, Sanctity (+15 hp, existing monks too), Heresy, Illumination (recharge x2), Block Printing (+3 range, 117 here), Theocracy (only the converter rests), Faith (attempts 6-14; the reference's per-attempt chance with Faith is unverified). Costs from the reference; research time design_default 20 s. Fervor (+15% speed: movement per tick must divide 50) and Herbal Medicine (no garrison) not implemented.

Only monks carry them (relic command), a carrier cannot convert, a killed carrier drops it where it fell, deposit into an own finished monastery (max 10); a razed monastery leaves them on the ground (design). Remembered relics can be ordered without leaking fog; nothing is built over a relic.
